verdicts.reason: Quote states the width, range and wrap of the binary pointer. The range and width are checkable only if the pointers are visible as signals, but the rule is fine as an assertion on the pointer. Keep content; the actor is a design element, not 'system'.
Quote states the address is the low bits of the binary pointer, truncating the MSB. Checkable.
Quote states gray = bin XOR (bin>>1) and one-bit change per increment. Checkable.
Quote states the Gray-to-binary conversion formula. Checkable.

The occupancy estimate may differ from true occupancy only by pointer updates inside the synchronizer. This needs a model of synchronizer latency and is not checkable every cycle from interface signals. Use a scenario.
Only describes the data word width and encoding ('no interpretation'). Nothing to verify or exercise.
Only a description of flag width and polarity. It is not a verifiable behavior on its own.
Describes a design/coding convention (unsigned 4-state, no signed arithmetic). Nothing to verify or exercise in simulation.

questions.question: Are the binary pointer, Gray pointer and synchronized pointer signals observable at the interface or only internal? This decides whether AF-9-01 to AF-9-04 can be asserted from interface signals.
What is the exact synchronizer latency (number of stages) used to bound the pessimism of the occupancy estimate?
